rules: A claim is the smallest capability cell we can test: backend/version + mode + subject selector + destination evidence + transport + lifecycle operation + environment.
disposition supported_installed requires evidence_level installed or real_workflow with a dated result on that environment. Unit, component or CI-runner evidence never promotes a claim to supported.
last_result.result is what the named test actually reported in the named run. not_run means nobody has run it; it is not a pass.
A claim with an open defect cannot be supported_installed, whatever its tests say.

environments.ci-ubuntu-26.04-x86_64: GitHub-hosted runner image ubuntu-26.04 (20261021.618), kernel 7.0.0-1017-azure x86_64, cgroup2fs, nftables 1.1.6, run as root in a network namespace lab. Not an installed package, not systemd-launched.
environments.ci-macos-26: GitHub-hosted macos-26 runner, Xcode 26, unsigned builds; no system extension activated.
environments.ci-node-22: GitHub-hosted ubuntu runner, Node 22, controller tests against the Rust moatctl binary.
environments.unit: cargo test on any host; no OS hooks.
environments.omarchy-installed: Robert's Omarchy (Arch) machine with the packaged moatd systemd unit. No result recorded yet.
environments.mac-signed-installed: A signed, notarized install on a real Mac with the system extension approved. No result recorded yet.
environments.ci-ubuntu-installed-unit: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner with the packaged moatd.service installed and started by systemd, a real non-root user and home (linux/tests/installed-unit.sh). An installed unit on Ubuntu, not the Arch package on Omarchy.

claims.capability: policy schema validation (moat.policy.v1), unknown fields rejected
claims.limits: Pure semantics. Says nothing about any endpoint enforcing the policy.

claims.capability: precedence: safety > emergency (deny) > override (allow) > explicit (deny beats allow) > profile default
claims.limits: First-match profile order is documented and reorders are classified as broadening; overlapping profiles are allowed.

claims.capability: policy diff classifies every change that can permit previously denied traffic as broadening
tests: core/moat-core/tests/broadening_differential.rs (2000 random policy edits per run, exhaustive flow universe)
claims.limits: Conservative: hostname wildcard subsumption and set-content reasoning are syntactic, so some safe edits are reported as broadening. The signer (Lane B) still parses the human 'new allow rule' strings; it should switch to the structured changes field.

claims.capability: rules needing an unsupported capability are rejected or (allows that opt in) omitted with a report
claims.limits: Profiles are capability-checked: unsupported deny profiles fail compilation; other unsupported profiles are omitted only when the fallback is at least as strict. Linux backend id collisions are rejected. Device-targeted compiles (issue #26) skip rules/profiles whose device scope excludes every targeted device; the snapshot binds its device list and endpoints refuse a snapshot that does not name them. Controller adoption of per-device compiles is Lane B.

claims.capability: Ed25519 signed snapshots, platform match, replay rejection, expiry
claims.limits: policy_digest is canonical JSON; report.effective_digest binds base + overlays + compiler. Signatures cover the exact payload bytes.

claims.capability: temporary grants keep device, process-generation, session and task scope from approval to endpoint
claims.limits: Core keeps device, process-instance and task scope through grant -> rule -> snapshot JSON -> evaluation. The controller plans grants as moat.grant.v1 objects, the signer compiles them with moatctl compile --grants and decides from diff.changes[] and per-grant approvals; process scope needs process_enforcement, which no backend has, so process grants are refused by the controller and signer. Ordinary-app grants on Linux are omitted by the compiler and reported as not_enforceable. Unit/integration evidence only; no installed endpoint has exercised a grant yet.

claims.capability: protected-session enforcement for direct IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP egress (cgroup v2 socket match in an nftables inet output chain)
claims.limits: Run by the test script as root, not by the installed systemd service. Omarchy kernel untested. New packets of established flows hit the rule; no conntrack flush.

claims.capability: a contained caller cannot obtain a less restricted session through the moatd control socket
claims.limits: Kernel-attested callers only (SO_PEERCRED + SCM_CREDENTIALS mapped to cgroup v2, PID-reuse guarded). A contained caller may launch only its own profile with full broker isolation and close only its own sessions. Run as root in a CI netns lab, not through the installed systemd unit (W11). External pre-existing brokers (docker socket, ssh-agent, writable files) are outside this claim.

claims.capability: hostname rules for TCP in protected sessions via the session egress proxy (TLS SNI / HTTP CONNECT / Host)
claims.limits: Names are authorized before any proxy DNS lookup (lab resolver saw no query for forbidden names). Admitted streams are re-checked on every install and tick and end at expiry (measured 1.15 s after the deadline, 1 s tick), on a denying revision (0.80 s), task close (0.13 s), isolation (0.37 s) and daemon stop (0.11 s); post-decision bytes are bounded by one tick plus socket buffers, not zero. Direct and proxied agree for IPv4/IPv6 at an independent receiver. Not the installed unit; workload-side DNS is governed by profile DNS rules; domain fronting and ECH outer names remain; UDP is IP-only; streams are not adopted across a daemon restart.

claims.capability: durable activation journal; timed trial with automatic rollback; replay high-water kept across rollback; restart stops (does not adopt) running sessions
claims.limits: Fault injection is in-process (FaultStore) plus one real disk-full episode on a small tmpfs in CI netns. Not run under the installed systemd unit or on Omarchy; a power cut between the kernel update and the journal commit is reconciled by the documented restart path, not proven on hardware.

claims.capability: sequenced event spool with restart and gap markers and quota
claims.limits: Spool events do not yet carry the W01 event envelope (boot, clock uncertainty, producer authority).

claims.capability: inventory of ordinary (non-launcher) application traffic on Linux
claims.limits: Not implemented. W09 experiment and W10 decide the collector.

claims.capability: per-application rules for ordinary Linux apps
claims.limits: nftables cannot match executables; app rules are rejected at compile (allows that opt in are omitted with a report).

claims.capability: installed moatd systemd unit launches a workload that can edit its intended project while containment holds
claims.limits: Proven on an Ubuntu runner with the packaged unit under systemd, not on Omarchy: stays unproven until the Arch package runs there. The unit keeps CAP_SYS_PTRACE to open /proc/1/ns/mnt (decision pending: docs/decisions/W11-cap-sys-ptrace.md).

claims.capability: per-app outbound decisions in the NEFilterDataProvider system extension
claims.limits: Never run as a signed, approved system extension. Owned by Lane B (macos/); listed here so the ledger is complete.

claims.capability: live web actions show endpoint-backed status; notifications open the exact incident
claims.limits: Owned by Lane B (W08). Live mode still reuses demo success behavior and incident references can open the wrong incident.

claims.capability: coexistence with Tailscale / Surfshark and similar

defects.summary: Profile selection is implicit first match in list order; overlapping profiles are accepted.
Reordering overlapping profiles changes which default applies but is not classified as broadening.
Shortening a deny's expiry is classified as narrowing.
Changes to fields the diff does not inspect are not classified as broadening.
Unsupported restrictive profiles compile and silently fall back.
Digests use implementation serialization, not a specified canonical form; the effective digest excludes overlays.
defects.closed_by: W03 core (compile::policy_digest canonical JSON; report.effective_digest = base + overlays + compiler)

defects.summary: Generated grants lose device and process-generation scope. Core renders moat.grant.v1 -> exact rule (W03 core); the controller no longer renders grants (grantToml and reserved device groups removed) and publishes with moatctl compile --grants.
defects.closed_by: W03 controller/signer (controller/src/controller.ts planGrant/publish, signer.ts sign, moatctl.ts compile --grants)
regression_tests: controller/test/grants.test.ts: two devices with the same executable never share a single-device exception
controller/test/grants.test.ts: grants are moat.grant.v1 objects compiled by `moatctl compile --grants`; a base change supersedes them
controller/test/grants.test.ts: the signer enforces the delegation's own limits independently of the controller

defects.summary: A retried grant request mints a fresh expiry. The controller follows GrantLedger semantics: same idempotency key + same request returns the original plan/grant and admission_until; same key + different request is refused (409).
defects.closed_by: W03 controller/signer (grant_plans.request_digest; signer journal by publication id)
regression_tests: controller/test/grants.test.ts: duplicate and lost requests keep the original deadline; a retry never mints a fresh lease
controller/test/grants.test.ts: a crash after signing (lost reply) recovers the same revision instead of a conflicting one

defects.summary: A contained caller can request a looser session through the control socket.
regression_tests: netns: W04 lab-deny workload cannot launch a lab-allow session via moat-launch
netns: W04 raw control-socket request from inside lab-deny refused
netns: W04 pre-opened outside connection used from inside lab-deny refused

defects.summary: A denied hostname can be resolved before authorization.
regression_tests: netns: W05 no DNS query left the host for a forbidden name (CONNECT, SNI, Host)

defects.summary: No stream registry; admission and stream expiry are not distinguished.
regression_tests: netns: W05 stream ended at expiry / deny / task close / isolation / daemon stop

defects.summary: Apply/rollback state is not journaled; storage failures are not fault-tested.
regression_tests: linux/moatd/src/endpoint/journal_faults.rs (12 fault-injection tests: disk full, failed rename, crash at every plain and trial step, backend error, torn commit, corrupt journal, corrupt replay mark, retained rollback intent, failed and crashed rollback, first canary, stop-not-adopt)
netns: W06 disk full refuses activation as not durable, prior revision stays enforced, same revision applies after space returns, restart confirms
netns: W06 spool records the session that was not adopted across the restart

defects.summary: Packaged systemd restrictions break launched coding workloads.
defects.closed_by: W11 (linux/moatd/src/launch.rs host mount namespace step; linux/packaging/systemd/moatd.service; docs/decisions/W11-cap-sys-ptrace.md)
regression_tests: installed-unit: W11: the workload wrote its intended project under $HOME (not the service's read-only view)
installed-unit: W11: the workload's /tmp is the user's real /tmp, not the service's PrivateTmp
installed-unit: containment: egress denied / cgroup escape fails / broader nested launch refused, before and after systemctl restart

defects.summary: Mac cache, trust reload, first canary and stale status gaps.
Live web actions reuse demo success behavior.
A notification reference can open the wrong incident.
A device-scoped rule (app-scoped block, hostname block on a Mac) was refused for the whole fleet because the compiler checked every rule against every platform in the fleet (issue #26).
